key_insight: A SCAPS-1D + machine learning workflow can rapidly rank multilayer perovskite solar-cell stacks and identify high-efficiency, lead-free designs without exhaustively simulating every combination.
engineering_relevance: The study provides a practical optimization framework for selecting ETL, absorber, and HTL materials that can accelerate device design and reduce trial-and-error in perovskite photovoltaics.
method: Trained an ML model on a representative subset to predict PCE for unseen stacks.
Used SHAP to identify the most influential descriptors for performance.
evidence_signal: Leave-One-Group-Out cross-validation showed reliable ranking via Spearman correlation, and the top ML-predicted structures were confirmed by full SCAPS-1D simulations, including FTO/TiO2/Cs2AgBiBr6/NiO/Ag at 28.85% PCE.
watch_item: The model’s recommendations depend on the quality and coverage of the simulated training set, so unexplored chemistry or imperfect device assumptions could limit real-world transferability.
paper_title: Multilayer Screening of Double and Conventional Perovskite Solar Cells Using SCAPS-1D and Machine Learning: Optimization of ETL, HTL, and Absorber for High-Efficiency Architectures
